The goal is to merge our two datasets. On one side, we have the AMOBIO dataset
that contains information about the impact of dams and nutrients for the
biological stations. On the other hand, we have the ASPE dataset that contains
the information about the state of the fish community at the stations.

## Setup

```{r}
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)
library(ggplot2)
library(hrbrthemes)
library(dplyr)
library(riversea)
library(sf)
riversea::nice_theme()
```

From ASPE data, we want to extract information about the food web structure, and
the fishing operation (ID, date, sandre code). Here is the structure of the
dataframe we get.

```{r}
web <- get(base::load(here("data", "river", "output_size2webs.rda")))
metrics <- web$tab_local_foodwebs_summary_metrics |>
  mutate(operation_id = as.integer(operation_id))

size <- get(base::load(here("data", "river", "output_individual_fish.rda")))
operation_sandre <- left_join(
  size$fishing_operation |> select(operation_id, site_id, date),
  size$station |> select(site_id, sandre_code),
  by = join_by(site_id)
)

aspe_data <- metrics |>
  left_join(operation_sandre, by = join_by(operation_id))
str(aspe_data)
```

## Map trophic structure

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 7

amobio_data <- tar_read(combined_amobio_data)

data <- amobio_data |>
  inner_join(aspe_data, by = join_by(sandre_code, date))

riversea::plot_amobio_metric(
  data,
  "S",
  year = 2019,
  title = "Species richness",
  subtitle = "Year 2019.",
  legend = "S"
)

riversea::plot_amobio_metric(
  data,
  "C",
  year = 2019,
  title = "Connectance",
  subtitle = "Year 2019.",
  legend = "C"
)

riversea::plot_amobio_metric(
  data,
  "maxTL",
  year = 2019,
  title = "Max. trophic level",
  subtitle = "Year 2019.",
  legend = "max TL"
)
```

## Link food web structure to environment


```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(data, aes(x = elevation, y = S)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.01) +
  labs(
    x = "Elevation [m]", 
    y = "Species richness",
    title = "Richness and elevation",
    subtitle = "All years put together."
  )

ggplot(data, aes(x = log10(poe_ddam_l3_dam), y = S)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05) +
  geom_smooth() +
  labs(
    x = "Distance to closest dam [km]", 
    y = "Species richness",
    title = "Dam proximity and richness",
    subtitle = "Downstream distance. All years put together."
  )

ggplot(data, aes(x = log10(poe_ddam_l2_dam), y = S)) +
geom_point(alpha = 0.05) +
  geom_smooth() +
  labs(
    x = "Distance to closest dam [km]", 
    y = "Species richness",
    title = "Dam proximity and richness",
    subtitle = "Upstream distance. All years put together."
  )
```

## Statistical models


```{r}
library(INLA)

data_inla <- data |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(lubridate::year(date)),
    site_id = as.integer(sandre_code),
    log_dist_dam_up_std = scale(poe_ddam_l3_dam),
    log_dist_dam_down_std = scale(poe_ddam_l2_dam),
    log_phosphorus_std = scale(pc_n_ptotal_s1_1y),
    elevation_std = scale(elevation)
  ) |>
  select(
    S,
    year,
    site_id,
    log_dist_dam_up_std,
    log_dist_dam_down_std,
    log_phosphorus_std,
    elevation_std
  ) |>
  tidyr::drop_na()

m_S <- inla(
   S ~ log_dist_dam_up_std + log_dist_dam_down_std + log_phosphorus_std +
    elevation_std +
    f(site_id, model = "iid") +
    f(year, model = "iid"),
  family = "nbinomial",
  data = data_inla
)

summary(m_S)
```
